## Introduction

`sdvplotR` provides a unified interface for visualizing sports data across multiple leagues in the SportsDataverse ecosystem. This article walks you through the core features of the package.

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Valid Teams

Before plotting, you can list a league's teams and the identifiers that are valid for them:

```{r valid-names}
# Get all NFL team abbreviations
nfl_teams <- sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr
head(nfl_teams)

# Get team names instead of abbreviations
nfl_team_names <- sdv_teams("nfl")$name
head(nfl_team_names)

# The 28 leagues of the team index
sdv_leagues()
```

## Identifiers from any source

Team identifiers come in many spellings: an nflverse abbreviation, a school
name from CollegeFootballData.com, an ESPN team id. `sdv_resolve()` turns any
of them into the index's canonical team id, and every helper that takes a team
does the same internally:

```{r resolve}
# an nflverse abbreviation, a full name and an ESPN team id: one team
sdv_resolve(c("KC", "Kansas City Chiefs", "12"), league = "nfl")

# a CFBD school name
sdv_resolve("Ohio State", league = "cfb")

# a typo does not resolve; sdv_suggest() proposes candidates
sdv_suggest("Kansas Cty", league = "nfl", n = 3)
```

The team index and logo archive are read from the SportsDataverse CDN and
cached for a day. `sdv_versions()` reports which data version is in use, and
`options(sdvplotR.offline = TRUE)` keeps everything on the copy bundled with the
package.

## Plotting Team Logos

The `geom_sdv_logos()` function plots team logos at specified coordinates:

```{r logos-basic, eval=FALSE}
# Create sample data
df <- data.frame(
  x = rep(1:4, 4),
  y = sort(rep(1:4, 4), decreasing = TRUE),
  team = sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr[1:16]
)

# Plot logos
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = team), league = "nfl", width = 0.075) +
  theme_void()
```

## Using Team Colors

Map team names to their official colors using the color scales:

```{r colors, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Bar chart of example values for NFL teams, each bar filled and outlined in the team's primary and secondary colors."}
df <- data.frame(
  team = sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr[1:8],
  value = runif(8, 0, 1)
)

ggplot(df, aes(x = team, y = value)) +
  geom_col(aes(color = team, fill = team), width = 0.5) +
  scale_color_sdv(league = "nfl", which = "secondary") +
  scale_fill_sdv(league = "nfl", alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Theme Elements

Replace axis labels with logos using theme elements. Add them after a complete
theme such as `theme_minimal()`; set on `axis.text.x` (or `axis.text.y`), they
also replace the `axis.text.x.bottom` (`axis.text.y.left`) element that theme
sets:

```{r theme-elements, eval=FALSE}
df <- data.frame(
  team = sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr[1:8],
  value = runif(8, 0, 1)
)

ggplot(df, aes(x = team, y = value)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = team), width = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_sdv(league = "nfl", alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_sdv_logo(league = "nfl"))
```

## Player Headshots

Plot player headshots using their ESPN athlete IDs:

```{r headshots, eval=FALSE}
# NFL player GSIS IDs
df_players <- data.frame(
  x = 1:3,
  y = 3:1,
  player_id = c("00-0033873", "00-0026498", "00-0035228"),
  player_name = c("P. Mahomes", "M. Stafford", "K. Murray")
)

ggplot(df_players, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_sdv_headshots(aes(player_id = player_id), league = "nfl", id_system = "gsis", height = 0.2) +
  geom_label(aes(label = player_name), nudge_y = -0.35) +
  theme_void()
```

## gt Tables

Add logos to gt tables:

```{r gt-tables, eval=FALSE}
library(gt)

df_table <- data.frame(
  team = sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr[1:8],
  logo = sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr[1:8],
  wins = sample(1:16, 8)
)

df_table |>
  gt() |>
  gt_sdv_logos(columns = "logo", league = "nfl")
```

## Team Tier Plots

Create tier plots for any league:

```{r tier-plots, eval=FALSE}
team_abbrs <- sample(sdv_teams("nfl")$abbr)
df_tiers <- data.frame(
  tier_no = sample(1:5, length(team_abbrs), replace = TRUE),
  team = team_abbrs
)

sdv_team_tiers(df_tiers, league = "nfl")
```

## Working with Multiple Sports

The same functions work across all supported leagues:

```{r multi-sport, eval=FALSE}
# NBA logos
nba_df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:5,
  y = 5:1,
  team = sdv_teams("nba")$abbr[1:5]
)

ggplot(nba_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = team), league = "nba", width = 0.075) +
  theme_void()

# CFB logos
cfb_df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:5,
  y = 5:1,
  team = sdv_teams("cfb")$abbr[1:5]
)

ggplot(cfb_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = team), league = "cfb", width = 0.075) +
  theme_void()
```

## Every league

`sdv_leagues()` lists all 28 leagues of the team index, from the NFL and the
Premier League to the junior hockey leagues, NCAA softball and cricket. The
loop below draws ten teams of each that have a logo, one row per league. It reads the team list
from the snapshot bundled with the package (`sdvplotR.offline`), so it does not
wait on a live fetch of the index.

```{r every-league, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 12, fig.alt = "Ten team logos for each of the 28 leagues of the SportsDataverse team index, one labelled row per league, from the AAF and AHL to the XFL."}
op <- options(sdvplotR.offline = TRUE)
teams <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sdv_leagues(), function(lg) {
  t <- sdv_teams(lg)
  # sdv_logo_url() warns for teams with no archived logo; keep ten that have one
  t <- tail(t[!is.na(suppressWarnings(sdv_logo_url(t$team_id, lg))), ], 10)
  data.frame(league = lg, team = t$team_id, x = seq_len(nrow(t)))
}))
# geom_sdv_logos() takes one league per layer: one layer per league
layers <- lapply(split(teams, teams$league), function(d) {
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(x = x, y = 0, team = team), data = d, league = d$league[1], width = 0.08)
})
ggplot() +
  layers +
  facet_wrap(~league, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 10.5)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )
options(op)
```
